1.explanation: The CSS-extras plugin (prism-css-extras.js and its minified counterpart) extends the core CSS grammar with a rule to tokenize “!important”. Its current regex only matches when “!important” is preceded by whitespace or other delimiters. Declarations like “value!important” lack that delimiter, so the token rule never fires. Updating the regex in these files to allow matching “!important” without a leading space (for example by making the look-behind optional or by matching /!important\b/ globally) will fix the bug.
1.bug_scenario:
When you write a CSS declaration with “!important” immediately after the value—without any intervening space—Prism does not recognize “!important” as a separate token. For example:

  • ul{position:absolute!important}   ← “!important” is rendered as part of the value
  • <div style="position:relative!important;"> …  ← again not highlighted as the “important” token

However, if you add a space before the exclamation mark (e.g. “position: relative !important”), Prism’s CSS‐extras plugin will pick it up correctly. The root cause is the regular expression in the CSS‐extras component, which only matches “!important” when it follows whitespace or certain punctuation. “Absolute!important” (no space) thus fails.

2.explanation: The core CSS grammar in prism-css.js defines the pattern for matching the “!important” token. In the current implementation the regular expression requires a whitespace or start‐of‐string before the exclamation mark (e.g. /(^|\s)!important\b/), so “!important” glued directly to a value (no space) isn’t matched. To fix it, the pattern should be simplified to /!important\b/, allowing the parser to recognize “!important” regardless of surrounding whitespace. Both the source file (prism-css.js) and its minified counterpart must be updated.
2.bug_scenario: When highlighting CSS code with Prism, a declaration like “position:absolute!important;” (no space before “!important”) is not correctly tokenized. Instead of splitting the value and the “!important” flag, Prism treats “absolute!important” as a single plain text token. When there is a space before “!important” (e.g. “position: absolute !important”), Prism recognizes and highlights the flag correctly.
